about: Original questions written for this project. Their style is inspired by the official quizzes (Wizarding World sorting quiz: dilemmas, objects and 'which would you hate'; Divergent aptitude test: moral scenarios like the growling dog and the stranger on the bus; Pokémon GO team leaders' philosophies; Avatar nations' cultural values). No question is copied from those quizzes. Each option carries 2 hidden trait words, which are the only thing BERT sees, and a 'key': what WE, the designers, expect in each world. A null key means we expect no clear group. The key is the 'official-test-style' score and is compared against BERT's answer.

questions.text: A stray dog is growling at a child in a park. What do you do?

options.text: Step between them and hold your ground.
Freeze and read the dog's body language first.
Scoop up the child and wave the owner over.
Crouch down and offer the dog some of your food.

questions.inspired_by: Divergent aptitude test (the stranger who asks about someone you know)
questions.text: An upset stranger asks whether you know a certain person. You do. What do you say?

options.text: "Yes. Why do you want to know?"
"No." It isn't your place to hand someone over.
"Not sure." Then you quietly warn the person later.
You ask what happened, and maybe help them sort it out.

questions.inspired_by: Sorting-quiz style: 'which would you most hate to be called'
questions.text: Which of these would sting the most if someone said it about you?

options.text: "You're so ordinary."
"You only think about yourself."
"You don't know what you're talking about."
"You backed down."

questions.text: You suddenly have a free afternoon. What do you do with it?

options.text: Go somewhere you've never been, without a plan.
Get lost reading about something obscure.
Help a friend move apartments.
Work on a side project you hope will pay off one day.

questions.text: You can take only one thing on a long journey. Which one?

options.text: A worn notebook full of half-finished ideas.
A sturdy pocketknife.
A letter from someone who loves you.
A key to a door you haven't opened yet.

questions.inspired_by: Pokémon GO team leaders' philosophies (strength vs. analysis vs. instinct)
questions.text: Your team is losing with five minutes left. What do you do?

options.text: Push everyone to go all-out. There's still time.
Call a timeout and change the plan.
Keep everyone's spirits up, win or lose.
Do whatever it takes, even if it bends the rules.

questions.inspired_by: Divergent factions' values (honesty vs. peace vs. knowledge)
questions.text: Someone criticizes your work in front of others, and they're partly right. How do you react?

options.text: Admit the part they got right and argue the rest openly.
Say thanks, then redo it so well nobody can say anything.
Let it go. Staying calm matters more than winning.
Take notes and think it over alone later.

questions.inspired_by: Avatar nations' cultural values (community, endurance, freedom, drive), with no element words
questions.text: Which place feels most like home?

options.text: A crowded kitchen where everyone talks at once.
A quiet library late at night.
A rooftop with a view over the whole city.
A training ground at sunrise.

questions.inspired_by: Sorting-quiz style moral dilemma (loyalty vs. truth)
questions.text: You find out a close friend cheated on an important exam. What do you do?

options.text: Tell them to come clean, or you will.
Say nothing. They're your friend.
Try to understand why they felt they had to.
Remember it. It might be useful someday.

questions.text: Pick a superpower you would actually use every day.

options.text: Knowing what people really think.
Never feeling fear.
Healing anyone you touch.
Changing anyone's mind in a few words.

questions.inspired_by: Pokémon GO team leaders (gut feeling vs. evidence vs. strength)
questions.text: When you make a big decision, what do you trust most?

options.text: My gut, even when I can't explain it.
The evidence, once I have enough of it.
What the people I care about need.
Whatever gets me closer to my goal.

questions.text: In group projects, which role do you usually end up in?

options.text: The one who keeps everyone getting along.
The one who says what nobody wants to hear.
The one who quietly does the parts nobody wants.
The one who presents it at the end.

free_text.text: Optional: describe yourself in a few words, the way a friend would.
free_text.placeholder: e.g. stubborn but kind, always late, asks too many questions
